summary:
Radar for 2026-11-12, GLP-1 focus only. The biggest fresh event is the FDA's class-wide NAION (rare optic-nerve "eye stroke") label warning, announced Nov 9. Every major outlet has covered it (AP, CBS, NBC, Reuters, WSJ, BBC, Guardian, CNBC, Forbes, AAO), but calm tirzepatide-specific explainers that work from the label are still scarce. That makes it the top label-change long-form. The FDA's numbers are 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years. Frame it as a rare, possible risk, with clear "sudden vision loss means get urgent care" guidance and no stop advice.

The second fresh hook is a Nature paper (Nov 11): rare GLP1R variants were linked to less weight loss on semaglutide but not on tirzepatide. It's an emerging tirzepatide-first angle. It's genetic and association-level, so it fits a careful Short, not a long-form.

Seasonal timing favours Thanksgiving (peak Nov 18–27; hold Shorts until Nov 18) and holiday travel with the pen (storage and flying, per the Instructions for Use).

Practical tirzepatide topics (Lane A) stay the backbone and line up with the playbook queue: injection-site reactions and the injection-site how-to, dehydration, burping and heartburn, nausea, a "what to expect" timeline, keeping results after stopping, and repackaging hair loss.

Foundayo (orforglipron) ATTAIN-OSA Phase 3 results came out Nov 9. Use them to refresh a label-only "Foundayo: what to expect" video for an approved drug that people search for. The sleep apnea use isn't approved.

Things I checked and downgraded:
- REDEFINE 4 (CagriSema vs tirzepatide) was already reported Feb–Apr 2026. It only counts as a fast-turn video if ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17) brings genuinely new randomized data against tirzepatide.
- The "stopping Mounjaro triggers psychiatric symptoms" headlines rest on weak sourcing. The FDA's Jan 2026 meta-analysis of 91 trials found no increased psychiatric risk. Mention it only as context inside the stopping video, never as a hook.
- The resistance-training RCT (Nat Med, Nov 9) is solid. Our own "lifting RCT" Short got only 13 views, so use it as a funnel Short pointing to the Strength and Bones videos.

Rejected: compounded-tirzepatide price reports, Hims & Hers/Ro telehealth deal stories, "research-use" tirzepatide vials, and gray-market retatrutide.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) and the FDA's new NAION vision warning: what the label change says, how rare it is (FDA: 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years), symptoms that need urgent care
candidates.angle: Label-change explainer in a calm, 'you just saw the headline' tone. What NAION is, why the FDA calls it a 'potential' risk, what changed in Warnings and Precautions for tirzepatide specifically, and the one rule: sudden vision loss in one eye means urgent care right away. Then talk to your prescriber; don't stop on your own. Open with a 'you' scenario (a scary push notification), give the rarity number by 15 s, and put a second payoff (the symptom checklist) by 30 s. Name NANOS and the AAO. Keep 'potential' and 'rare' everywhere.
candidates.predicted_peak: now to 10 days (search for 'mounjaro vision' keeps rising as patients get updated labels and pharmacy inserts)
candidates.why_now: The FDA ordered class-wide labelling on Nov 9 and coverage is still spreading (AP, CBS, NBC, WSJ, BBC, Guardian, USA Today, AAO explainer Nov 11, local TV Nov 12). This is the label-change format the owner flagged as a 10x–195x search format. Mainstream outlets cover 'GLP-1s' generically, and very few calm tirzepatide-specific, label-based videos exist. Our earlier news-only NAION Short got 34 views, so package this as a body-worry question, not news.

evidence.signal: FDA requires class-wide GLP-1 RA labelling for potential NAION risk, tirzepatide included
NAION warning added across the class; prescribers advised to consider stopping if NAION is confirmed
FDA figures: 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years

evidence.source: Google News: AAO, Forbes, Guardian, CBS, AP (Nov 9–12)
evidence.signal: More than 40 mainstream and local outlets in 72 h

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions and how to choose and rotate injection sites (per the Zepbound/Mounjaro Instructions for Use): redness, itching, small lumps; label rates 6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo; when to call
candidates.angle: Device how-to plus 'is this normal?'. Cover the three IFU-listed areas (stomach, thigh, back of upper arm, with the arm site done by someone else), why rotating helps, what a normal reaction looks like, and the red flags (spreading redness, signs of allergic reaction: get help right away). IFU wording only, with no amounts or dosing. A proven repeat theme for us.
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; refreshed by holiday-season new starts in Dec–Jan
candidates.why_now: This is first in the Lane A queue. Our injection-site Shorts reached 242 views and 129 by day 1–2, and device how-tos are a format the owner flagged. Constant search demand from new starters, and most YouTube coverage is either brand IFU or casual vlogs.

evidence.signal: Seen 5+ times, momentum 87–89
Label injection-site reaction rates by dose vs placebo

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, protein first, smaller portions, eating slowly, and easing nausea at a big holiday meal
candidates.angle: A practical 'your plate on tirzepatide' walkthrough. Why slower gastric emptying makes big holiday meals feel different, the eating-order and portion moves that help, and when nausea or vomiting means calling your prescriber. Shorts are funnel Shorts pointing to the existing Thanksgiving long-form.
candidates.why_now: Seasonal peak in 6–15 days. Seen in 11 straight snapshots. The Thanksgiving long-form is climbing (93 min, up from 17). The playbook says hold Thanksgiving Shorts until Nov 18 (the Nov 6 one got 21 views).

evidence.signal: Seen in 11 snapshots, momentum 89→93
GLP-1 users are changing what they buy and eat, not just how much

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide what to expect: a week-by-week and month-by-month timeline (appetite changes, common GI side effects easing, average trial weight-loss curve in SURMOUNT-1)
candidates.angle: A 'what to expect' timeline from the label and SURMOUNT-1 (adults with obesity, without diabetes). Cover what people commonly notice early, when GI side effects tend to ease, and how the average curve keeps going down through 72 weeks. Results vary, with no dosing or titration details. End with questions to ask your prescriber. A natural 'watch next' feeder into Side Effects and How Long.
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; surges with New Year starts (late Dec–Jan)
candidates.why_now: The owner named 'what to expect' timelines as a top search format. The How Long video already earns suggested traffic, and holiday and New Year starters will search this heavily in 6–8 weeks, so publishing now lets it rank first.

evidence.signal: What-to-expect timelines beat their channels' usual views by 10x–195x in this niche
Steady consumer demand for Mounjaro/Zepbound timeline content

candidates.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide: SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335; +14.0% regain on placebo, yet still 9.9% below starting weight), why regain varies, and the habits linked to holding on
candidates.angle: Hopeful and evidence-based. What SURMOUNT-4 actually showed in both arms, why stopping is a plan to make with your prescriber, and the habits with evidence behind them (strength training, protein, sleep, follow-up). Mention the 'stopping causes psychiatric symptoms' headlines only to say the FDA's Jan 2026 meta-analysis of 91 trials found no increased psychiatric risk, and that any mood change should go to a clinician.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
candidates.why_now: ACSH published '5 strategies to keep weight off if you stop' on Nov 12, and 'stopping Mounjaro' psychiatric-symptom stories are circulating (Nov 12), so search interest is fresh. Our Stopping video had an 8.9% CTR by day 5. Build a sibling video and link the two.

evidence.signal: 'Taking GLP-1s forever? 5 strategies to keep weight off if you stop'

evidence.source: Health and Me / India News Network (Nov 12)
evidence.signal: Stopping-psychiatric-symptom headlines circulating; weak sourcing
Consumer coverage of changes after stopping Mounjaro/Zepbound

candidates.topic: Why semaglutide may work less well for some people, and tirzepatide didn't show the same effect: rare GLP1R gene variants (Nature, Nov 11)
candidates.angle: Tirzepatide-first 'what's confirmed?' Short. Rare variants in the GLP-1 receptor gene were linked to less weight loss on semaglutide but not on tirzepatide, which acts on two receptors (GLP-1 and GIP). Say clearly that it's a genetic association, rare variants, no clinical test recommended, and no switching advice: if results are disappointing, talk to your prescriber. Pair with the April Nature finding that a GIPR variant predicted nausea on tirzepatide.
keywords: why ozempic doesn't work for me
candidates.why_now: Published in Nature on Nov 11 with almost no consumer coverage yet. 'Why isn't my GLP-1 working?' is a big, stable search question, and this gives it a fresh, tirzepatide-first hook. Tirzepatide-first head-to-head Shorts in obesity get 109–177 views for us.

evidence.signal: 'Rare GLP1R variants attenuate weight loss with semaglutide but not tirzepatide'
Earlier paper: GLP1R and GIPR variants linked to weight loss and to nausea on tirzepatide (self-reported data, modest effects)
Specialist pickup of the GLP-1 RA response genetics

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide pen and holiday travel: what the Instructions for Use say about leaving it out of the fridge, heat, freezing, and flying with it
candidates.angle: A device how-to for the travel season: storage rules in the Instructions for Use (refrigerated, the allowed room-temperature window, never frozen, protect from heat and light), carry-on vs checked bag, and what to do if a pen froze or got too hot (don't use it; call the pharmacy). No amounts.
keywords: can zepbound be left out of fridge
candidates.why_now: Holiday travel starts in about 10 days. Device how-tos are an owner-flagged 10x format, and the question spikes every holiday period. Few clean, IFU-based answers exist on YouTube.

evidence.signal: Pen storage for holiday travel at momentum 78, emerging
Storage and handling section and Instructions for Use

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide dehydration: signs to watch for and what helps (the label's warning about acute kidney injury linked to fluid loss from vomiting or diarrhoea)
candidates.angle: A practical hydration guide: why appetite suppression can mean drinking less, the warning signs (dizziness, dark urine, peeing less), easy habits, and when vomiting or diarrhoea means calling your prescriber. Holiday alcohol and travel make it timely without dating the video.
candidates.why_now: Second in the playbook's Lane A queue. The label anchor is solid. Recent ER-doctor and poison-centre GLP-1 stories (Nov 5–6) raised awareness.

evidence.signal: Warnings: acute kidney injury linked to dehydration from GI adverse reactions
'15 GLP-1 side effects, from most to least likely': mainstream interest in the side-effect ranking

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide nausea: why it happens, when it usually eases, and what helps (smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping when full, avoiding greasy food)
candidates.angle: A felt-symptom explainer: slower gastric emptying plus brain appetite signals. Label rates in the right population, what commonly helps, and when vomiting with severe stomach pain means calling your healthcare provider right away. Hook: a Nature study found a GIP-receptor gene variant predicted nausea on tirzepatide, a reason it varies from person to person (association only).
keywords: how to stop nausea on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: A top felt-symptom search the owner named directly. Our nausea Short got 180 views. Big holiday meals will push nausea searches up next week.

evidence.signal: GIPR variant linked to nausea and vomiting on tirzepatide but not semaglutide
'Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects': mainstream demand

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide burping and heartburn: why slower gastric emptying causes sulfur burps and reflux after big meals, and what helps
candidates.angle: A felt-symptom guide: the mechanism in one picture, the meal habits that commonly help (smaller portions, not lying down after eating, limiting fizzy and fatty foods), and when to see a doctor (trouble swallowing, chest pain: emergency number first).
candidates.why_now: In the playbook's Lane A queue and seen in 7 snapshots. Holiday meals make it more relevant. High search demand from people already on the medicine.

evidence.signal: Seen 7 times, momentum 76–80
GI adverse reactions, including dyspepsia and GERD, listed by dose

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) what to expect, refreshed by ATTAIN-OSA Phase 3 (Nov 9): about 44% fewer breathing interruptions without CPAP at 52 weeks; sleep apnea use not approved
candidates.angle: Search-led video on an approved drug, label only: what Foundayo is (a daily GLP-1 pill), how taking it differs from a weekly shot, common side effects, and what the new sleep apnea trial showed. Say plainly that Foundayo isn't approved for sleep apnea, while tirzepatide is approved for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. Questions to ask your doctor.
candidates.why_now: 'foundayo' is our top non-EloraTZP search term, and the orforglipron long has 262 min (111 from search). ATTAIN-OSA got Lilly, MedPage, TCTMD and Time coverage on Nov 9–10, and Lilly plans an FDA filing by the end of 2026. Lilly's celebrity patient campaign (Nov 10) is driving brand searches.

evidence.signal: ATTAIN-OSA: AHI −43.8% without PAP and −27.5% with PAP at 52 weeks; 31.5% reached remission or mild OSA
Lilly heads to FDA with the sleep apnea data
'GLP-1 Pill Shows Benefit in Sleep Apnea'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: will it grow back? (label: 5.4% vs 0.9% placebo; women 7.1% vs men 0.5%), plus why rapid weight loss can trigger temporary shedding
candidates.angle: Repackaging and relinking is the priority: support the retitled 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Hair Loss: Will It Grow Back?' with a new-angle Short (not growth or prevalence). For example, why shedding often shows up months after starting, and when to see a doctor (patchy loss, other symptoms). Only after the Hair long-form is verified clean.
candidates.why_now: Our hair grow-back Short has 1,025 views, the channel's best, while the Hair long-form sits at a 1.06% CTR. It's a packaging failure, not a demand failure. A felt symptom the owner named directly.

evidence.signal: Hair loss 5.4% vs 0.9% placebo, higher in women
Hair Short: 1,025 views; long-form: 1.06% CTR on 94 impressions

candidates.topic: Resistance training during tirzepatide: new randomized trial on keeping lean mass (Nat Med, Nov 9; UWA/RACGP coverage)
candidates.angle: Funnel Short to the Strength and Bones & Muscle long-forms. One new fact from the RCT, kept at its exact population (men and postmenopausal women aged 50–70 without diabetes, compared with usual activity, average results). Practical takeaway: lifting alongside the medicine; check with your clinician before a new exercise plan.
candidates.why_now: A fresh randomized trial in Nature Medicine (Nov 9), with RACGP newsGP and UWA pickup. Muscle loss on GLP-1s is a top worry. Our news-only 'lifting RCT' Short got 13 views, so frame it as a felt worry ('Will tirzepatide shrink my muscles?').

evidence.signal: 'Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: a randomized controlled trial'
'Resistance training slashes muscle loss for GLP-1 patients'

candidates.topic: ObesityWeek 2026 (Nov 14–17) watch: any fresh randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide, including the REDEFINE 4 full presentation (CagriSema 23.0% vs tirzepatide 25.5%, 84 weeks, open-label, 809 adults with obesity)

candidates.angle: A 'what's confirmed?' Short for the 13:00 lead slot. Pain and function results at the trial's exact scope (adults with obesity and knee OA, compared with placebo). State that it isn't approved anywhere and that online 'research' retatrutide isn't the trial drug. No approval-status title.

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide really quiet 'food noise'? What the evidence confirms (trial data on appetite and cravings) vs what's still murky
candidates.angle: A myth-vs-evidence funnel Short to the existing Food Noise long-form: randomized trials show less appetite and fewer cravings, but 'food noise' as a measured outcome is mostly qualitative so far. Avoid the survey result, since survey angles are banned.
candidates.why_now: Washington Times (Nov 11): 'evidence is murky'. Psychiatric Times reviewed it on Oct 28. It's a widely used phrase with steady search demand.

evidence.signal: 'Do GLP-1 drugs really quiet food noise? A new study says the evidence is murky'

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and gout: meta-analysis on uric acid and gout risk (Diabetes Obes Metab, Nov 8)
candidates.angle: Benefits beyond weight, at class scope ('GLP-1 medicines'). Report what the meta-analysis found on serum uric acid and gout, with the right hedges. Not a treatment for gout; ask your doctor.
candidates.why_now: A fresh meta-analysis with no consumer coverage yet. Gout is common in the audience, but it's a niche angle (niche angles underperform for us), so it ranks low.

evidence.signal: Systematic review and meta-analysis: GLP-1 RAs, hyperuricaemia, serum uric acid and gout
